what_its_for: Zonisamide is a seizure medicine (anticonvulsant) used to help control partial seizures in adults with epilepsy. It is often used along with other seizure medicines. Your doctor may also prescribe it for other conditions.
how_to_take: Take zonisamide by mouth with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, break, or chew it. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Drink 6 to 8 glasses of water every day while taking this medicine to help protect your kidneys and reduce the risk of kidney stones.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose, usually 100 mg once a day, and slowly increase it over several weeks. Most adults end up taking between 200 mg and 400 mg per day, but your doctor will decide the right dose for you. Never change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first — stopping suddenly can cause more seizures.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store zonisamide at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking zonisamide — it can increase dizziness and drowsiness and may worsen side effects. Be careful driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid getting overheated or dehydrated, especially in hot weather or during exercise, as zonisamide can reduce sweating and increase your risk of heat stroke. Avoid taking antacids containing carbonate or bicarbonate (like baking soda) without asking your doctor, as they may affect how the medicine works.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of suicide or depression, mood or behavior changes, decreased sweating or high body temperature (especially in children), skin rash, blisters, or peeling skin, signs of kidney stones such as severe back or side pain, blood in urine, or painful urination, signs of a serious blood problem such as fever, sore throat, mouth sores, or unusual bruising or bleeding, signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain, shortness of breath, or confusion. Also call your doctor if your seizures get worse or change.
when_it_works: Zonisamide may start to reduce seizures within a few weeks, but it can take 2 to 4 weeks or longer to feel the full benefit, especially since your doctor will slowly increase your dose. Keep taking it every day as directed, even if you feel well. Do not stop taking it on your own.
special_populations: Children: Zonisamide is not approved for children under 16 years old. Children may be at higher risk for decreased sweating and dangerous increases in body temperature — monitor closely if used in children. Older Adults (65+): Use with caution as side effects such as dizziness and confusion may be more common. Kidney or Liver Problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more closely. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Zonisamide may harm an unborn baby. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, as uncontrolled seizures can also be dangerous during pregnancy. Breastfeeding: Zonisamide passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding.
